correctness.rationale: Radial orthogonality gives ||z^n||²=1/(n+1)−q/(n+γ+1) and exact kernel c_n=(n+1)(n+γ+1)/((1−q)n+γ+1−q). For q<1 let p=1+γ/(1−q), μ_p=(p−1)u^{p−2}du; summation yields (1−q)(1−s)^2 K=1−q∫u[(1−s)/(1−us)]²dμ_p. The maximum-modulus bound u|(1−s)/(1−us)|²≤4u/(1+u)²<1 for 0<u<1 proves the disk and real-half-plane bounds. For q=0 equality is (1−s)^2K=1. For q=1 direct sum K=[(γ+1)+(1−γ)s]/[γ(1−s)^3] gives (1−s)^2K=1+(1+s)/(γ(1−s)), whose real part exceeds 1. Complete monomial basis follows radial Fourier orthogonality/Tonelli; |s|<1 ensures convergence.
